title: Photo 192 · 콜로설 · 마욜리카 · 쪼그려 앉기 정면 · 동아프리카 50대 후반
prompt:
Image format: a vertical portrait-orientation photograph, 2:3 aspect ratio, taller than it is wide.

A full-body photograph on a plain seamless mid-grey backdrop, nothing else in the frame, shot on a medium format camera with an 85mm lens at f/8, a single hard key light raking in from one side so the texture of the skin stands out, sharp focus from head to toe, realistic photographic grain — a real photograph, not an illustration, not CGI, not a render.

Subject: ONE real adult East African woman in her late 50s, lines at the eyes, mouth and neck, deep umber skin tone with a warm sheen, her face exactly the same tone as her body, real skin texture with visible pores and fine grain, long micro braids falling to her hips, a calm confident expression, real living eyes. She wears spiral drop earrings and has extra-long stiletto nails.

Physique: An extraordinarily large woman, far beyond any real person, her body so wide that her hips are cut off by the left and right edges of the frame. A giantess built on a completely even scale, every part of her enlarged by the same amount: massive rounded shoulders, huge thick arms, a colossal full bust, a broad heavy torso with a large smooth rounded belly, wide solid hips, enormous columnar thighs and thick heavy calves, a full round face. Her head looks small on top of her massive body, her shoulders span more than four head-widths, each hand is as wide as a normal woman's torso and each thigh thicker than a normal woman's waist. No single part stands out more than another, no hanging folds, not pregnant, her whole body scaled up together into one immense smooth silhouette that towers over the viewer. Every fold and curve keeps its own clear rounded outline with a deep shadowed crease between them, never merging into one shapeless mass. Her arms, hands, legs and feet stay in correct proportion to each other. The flesh is soft and loose at this age, every fold hanging low and settling deep over the one below it. The sheer weight of the flesh is visible in how it drops, compresses and presses out to the sides wherever two parts of her body meet.

Skin: Real photographic skin — visible pores and fine grain, coarse surface grain and fine crepey texture across the softest areas, natural creases and shadow where the flesh folds, faint stretch marks where the great curves have expanded, the raking light picking out every ridge and hollow of the surface. No smooth illustration finish, no plastic CG sheen.

Body Art: Her bare skin is painted in Italian maiolica tin-glaze style — a glossy warm cream glaze ground painted with cobalt blue, ochre yellow, copper green and manganese purple grotesque scrolls, acanthus leaves and medallions, a bold cobalt band following every deep crease and curving around the hips and thighs. The paint is pigment sitting on living skin, so it distorts slightly over every bulge and cracks a little where the skin folds. The paint covers her whole body with no bare skin left anywhere below the jaw: her shoulders, her upper arms, her forearms and the backs of her hands are painted as densely as her torso, and so are the sides of her body, her back, her rear, the lower belly, the knees, the calves and the tops of her feet. Her face is left unpainted and the pattern fades out at the neck with no hard line.

Pose: Squatting low facing the camera, balanced on the balls of her feet with the heels of her shoes lifted clear of the floor, her knees pushed wide apart by the bulk of her own thighs, her back straight and her torso upright, her calves squeezed flat beneath her thighs with the flesh of both bulging out where they meet, her hands resting on her knees with her arms held clear of her body so nothing crosses in front of her torso, her head level and facing the lens, full body head to feet filling the frame.

Footwear: Extreme cobalt-blue platform stiletto slides with a thick toe band, the platform soles as tall as her ankle bones, the ultra-thin stiletto heels so high her insteps stand nearly vertical.

Background & Lighting: the cobalt and ochre glowing on the cream glaze, the hard raking light carving every fold and curve.

Vertical 2:3 portrait-orientation full-body photograph, taller than it is wide.
